scope: Solar radiation at King's Park and Kau Sai Chau, sampled hourly from a one-minute feed, 2024-12 onward. Produced by scripts/ingest/fetch_hko_solar_1min.py. Added because the daily file next to it cannot answer three things: when during the day the sun reached the ground, how much of it arrived as direct beam rather than scattered, and whether one site represents the territory.

files.radiation_1min_hko.csv: One row per station per sampled hour: global, direct and diffuse radiation in W/m2, with the archive snapshot each reading came from.

relationship_to_radiation_hko.summary: Two radiation files sit in this directory, both from King's Park, overlapping on 576 days. They are not redundant and are not interchangeable.
relationship_to_radiation_hko.radiation_hko.csv: Daily totals in MJ/m2 from 2020. Use it for anything spanning seasons or years, and for day-level questions — it is the longer record and it is a true daily integral.
relationship_to_radiation_hko.radiation_1min_hko.csv: Hourly samples in W/m2 from 2024-12. Use it when the question is about time of day, about the direct/diffuse split, or about two stations. It is the shorter record and each value is an instant, not an integral.
relationship_to_radiation_hko.do_not: Do not sum this file's W/m2 values and compare the number to the daily file's MJ/m2 without converting: one hourly sample stands for 3600 s, so the sum times 3600/1e6 is the MJ/m2 equivalent. Done that way the two agree (see verification below); done naively they differ by three orders of magnitude.

sources.authority: Hong Kong Observatory (HKO), archived by DATA.GOV.HK
sources.title: Latest one-minute solar radiation, regional weather feed
sources.notes: HKO publishes only the latest reading — there is no historical endpoint for this feed. DATA.GOV.HK snapshots it about every ten minutes and keeps the snapshots, which is what makes a time series possible. The archive holds roughly 165 snapshots a day for this feed and begins in 2023; its `end` parameter is refused for any date later than yesterday, in plain text rather than JSON.

stations.name: King's Park
stations.note: Kowloon. Same site as the soundings and the daily radiation file.

stations.name: Kau Sai Chau
stations.note: Sai Kung, about 20 km east. The second site is what makes single-station representativeness measurable rather than assumed.

conventions.time: Hong Kong local standard time. The feed's own timestamp carries no timezone marker, so this was verified rather than assumed: the median diurnal cycle peaks at hour 12 and is zero at hours 0 and 6, which places it in local time — under UTC the peak would fall at hour 4.
conventions.sampling: One snapshot per hour, the first the archive holds in that hour, so a reading can sit up to about ten minutes after the hour it is filed under. Each value is an instantaneous one-minute mean, NOT an hourly average. `snapshot_time` records the snapshot each row came from. `--all-snapshots` rebuilds at the archive's full ~10-minute cadence for about six times the cost.
conventions.missing: Non-numeric placeholders in the feed become nulls rather than being dropped, so an out-of-service sensor stays visible as a gap.

verification.against_the_daily_file: Summing a day's hourly samples as W/m2 x 3600 s and comparing with the independent daily CIS totals over 577 complete days: r = 0.986, median ratio 1.002. This is the strongest check available, because the two files come from different HKO products by different routes.
verification.diurnal_cycle: Median global radiation is 0 at 06:00, peaks at 12:00, and returns to single digits by 18:00.
verification.completeness: 616 days spanned, 616 days present — no missing day. 23 to 25 samples per day (median 24).
verification.direct_diffuse_closure: Median ratio (direct + diffuse) / global = 1.000 across 12,134 daytime readings, but the interquartile range of the difference is -9 to +138 W/m2 and 944 of 29,284 readings (3.2 %) report diffuse strictly above global, which is impossible on a horizontal surface — 265 of them by more than 1 W/m2, the rest within instrument noise. See the first entry under known_limits.

known_features_that_are_not_errors: One reading of 1425 W/m2 exceeds the solar constant (1361 W/m2). It is internally consistent — direct 841 plus diffuse 594 — which is the signature of cloud enhancement, where the direct beam adds to bright scattering off cloud edges. Real, brief, and documented in the literature. 12 readings exceed 1200 W/m2 and 333 exceed 1000.

1,357 night-time readings sit between 1 and 12 W/m2 where zero is expected. They concentrate in summer (257 in July, 231 in June) and nearly vanish in winter (1 in November, 2 in October), which is the thermal-offset signature of a pyranometer exchanging infrared with the sky. Two to three orders of magnitude below daytime values; left in place rather than zeroed, because it is a property of the instrument and suppressing it would be deciding for the analyst.
known_limits: The direct column's reference plane is NOT established. Median (direct + diffuse) / global is exactly 1.000 over 12,134 daytime readings, which says direct is the horizontal component — but 29 % of readings overshoot global by more than 100 W/m2, those readings carry a mean direct of 585 against 264 overall, and the median deviation rises to +44 at 16:00 while sitting at -10 at noon. Rising overshoot at low sun with strong beam is the signature of normal-incidence direct, so the two conventions each have evidence and the data alone cannot decide. Use global_radiation_wm2 on its own, or the direct/diffuse pair only as a qualitative clear-versus-overcast indicator. Do NOT build a case that treats direct + diffuse as a decomposition of global; it does not reliably close.
Hourly samples, not hourly means. A passing cloud at the sampled minute moves the value in a way an hourly average would smooth.
Two sites, both of them meteorological stations rather than air-quality stations.
Begins 2024-12, so it cannot serve questions about earlier years; the daily file covers those.
